subject: Not able to successfully run inla formula

messages.author: 4d0b8e1d85fb683c
messages.subject: Not able to successfully run inla formula
parts:
Hi,

I'm using a mac Apple 11 macOS Ventura 13.5.2. I have installed R  (R version 4.3.2 (2023-10-31) ) and R studio from https://cran.rstudio.com/

I am experiencing problems with using INLA (short version shown below). Would you kindly help with this? 

Thank you!



# Filtering out for just 2020, and doing the above:
 data_inla_2020 <- filter(data_inla, year == 2020)
 colnames( data_inla_2020)
 
 # Creating a 1D mesh using X along the road: Road is assumed 1 dimensional so we use 1-d
 mesh_rutting_2020 <- inla.mesh.1d(loc = data_inla_2020$X, boundary = "free", offset = offset)
 
 # Creating the A-matrix: projection matrix; two inputs: mesh and locations
 A_rutting_2020 <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh_rutting_2020, loc = data_inla_2020$X.MID)
 
 
 # Making SPDE: using pcmatern (penalized complexity) allows us to use the range and sigma priors
 spde_2020 <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh_rutting_2020, prior.range = prior_range, prior.sigma = prior_sigma)
 
 # Making the index: give it a name of interest e.g., spatial.field.2020
 idx_2020 <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "spatial.field.2020", n.spde = spde_2020$n.spde)
 
 # Making the INLA stack: IMPORTANT: 1) data as list form (response variable), 2) A-matrix as a list including fixed effects (1), 3) index 4) prior on the intercept (if it is included in the model)
 stk_2020 <- inla.stack(data = list(rutting = data_inla_2020$rut.diff.response),
                        A = list(A_rutting_2020, 1),
                        effects = list(c(idx_2020, list(intercept = 1)),
                                       list(AADT1 = data_inla_2020$AADT.pt,
                                            road_cover = data_inla_2020$MASSETYPE_NEW,
                                            rut_depth = data_inla_2020$rut.depth.before,
                                            width1 = data_inla_2020$width,
                                            rut_depth2 = data_inla_2020$rut.depth.before_scaled,
                                            width2 = data_inla_2020$width_scaled)),
                        tag = "est_2020")
 
 # Creating the formula object:
 #formula_2020 <- rutting ~ -1 + intercept + road_cover + AADT1 + f(spatial.field.2020, model = spde_2020)
 formula_2020 <- rutting ~ -1 + road_cover : AADT1 + rut_depth2 : AADT1 + width2: AADT1 +
   f(spatial.field.2020, model = spde_2020)
 
 
 
 # Running INLA:
 res_2020 <- inla(formula = formula_2020,
                  data = inla.stack.data(stack = stk_2020, spde = spde_2020),
                  family = "gaussian",
                  control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk_2020), compute = TRUE), # IMPORTANT LINE, gives the posterior marginals as well
                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE), # extracts dic and wic
                  verbose = FALSE,
                  control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb", # integration step set to faster mode because of many hyperparameters
                                      strategy="gaussian",
                                      tolerance = 0.00001,
                                      restart=2,
                                      h = 0.0001)) # trouble shooting
 
 summary(res_2020)

error:

/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 65: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla: No such file or directory
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 71: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla: No such file or directory
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 71: exec: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla: cannot execute: No such file or directory

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Not able to successfully run inla formula
parts:
Hi,

this looks like an incomplete/failed install

can you remove the inla package, and then try to install it again ?

options(timeout=9999);
install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),
INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/testing"), 
dep=TRUE)
